lines: Now A.I. lets anyone send code in seconds.
Sending is free. But a person must check every one.
About a quarter are now low quality A.I. output.
PatchBond adds a small refundable deposit, like the one on a rental.
A stranger sends a change and pays under a dollar.
No payment in a day? It closes itself.
An A.I., sealed in a locked box, reads the work and signs its verdict.
Real work gets every cent back.
Clear slop loses its deposit to the project, and it can be disputed.
Flood a project, and your own price climbs.
A.I. agents pay too, with a key that only spends inside your limits.
On real pull requests, it took nothing from good work and caught only a few bad ones.
So the deposit is the filter, not the A.I.
PatchBond, on NEAR. Maintainers, try it free on testnet.
